text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The leaders of Union Bank and Tallinna Bank will meet today in an attempt to put an end to their mud-throwing in the newspapers.
- An old couple were discovered brutally killed on Friday in the Rannu district, Tartu county, police said.
- The new ferry Regula made its debut trip between the mainland and Saaremaa island on Saturday, with the prime minister and Riigikogu members aboard.
- Prime minister Mart Siimann said he would resign if parliament rejects the protective tariffs for imported pork.
- Estonia needs tanks for defence forces' training, the defence minister and commander of armed forces said.
- The planned summit of the Baltic Sea countries, which was scheduled to be held in Riga this summer, has been postponed because of a delay in preparations, a Swedish official said.
Estonia lost 1 - 3 to Latvia in a World Cup European group four qualifying match on Sunday.
